Passive consumption, distraction, the ego in an unconscious loop of input without processing
Documenting, capturing, attempting to fix experience: the desire to hold onto something fleeting

symbols.plain_language: Your connection to everyone and everything, in one small object. Phone dreams tend to be about reach: who you can and can't contact, what messages are waiting, what you keep checking. A dead battery or no signal often marks a connection in your life that's lost its charge.

symbols.name: Bed / Sleeping
symbols.core_meaning: The place of rest, dreams, intimacy, vulnerability, and unconsciousness. The bed is where you surrender the ego nightly. Dreams about beds are meta: the unconscious commenting on your relationship to sleep, rest, intimacy, or the unconscious itself.

variations.meaning: Your intimate, private self: the most personal space in the psyche
Unfamiliar intimacy, vulnerability in unknown territory, sleeping in someone else's psychic space
Intimate psychological merger: whose psychic space are you sharing? Coniunctio or enmeshment?
Consciousness refusing to rest: the ego unable to surrender to the unconscious even when it needs to

symbols.plain_language: Where you let your guard down. The bed holds rest, intimacy, illness, and dreaming itself, so a dream about a bed is often the psyche commenting on how surrender is going: whether you can rest, whether you feel safe enough to be held, what shares the bed with you.

symbols.name: Map / Compass
symbols.core_meaning: Orientation: the ego's attempt to know where it is and where it's going. The map represents the existing model of the psyche. Finding a map = discovering a framework for understanding yourself. Losing a map = being forced to navigate without a model.

variations.meaning: Using a framework to navigate the psyche: individuation with a guide, a therapist, or a companion like this site
The existing framework no longer works: you're beyond the mapped territory. Necessary disorientation.
Creating your own framework: making sense of territory through your own exploration
Inner direction: not a map but a sense of which way is true. The Self as compass pointing toward individuation.

symbols.plain_language: Knowing where you are. A map is your working model of the territory: finding one can mean a framework has arrived that finally makes the landscape make sense. Losing the map, or finding it wrong, often marks a season of navigating without one. That is a stage of every real journey.

symbols.name: Hands
symbols.core_meaning: Agency, the capacity to act, to create, to grasp, to hold, to release. What the hands DO in the dream reveals the ego's capacity for action and creation.

variations.meaning: Full agency: the capacity to act, create, and engage is intact
Agency restrained: something is preventing you from acting. What binds you?
Guilt, having done something that costs, responsibility for harm (real or projected)
Desire for connection, grasping for something just out of reach, the will to contact
Damaged capacity to act: the ability to create, work, or reach has been wounded
Connection, partnership, mutual support: the ego in relationship with another part of the psyche or another person

symbols.plain_language: What you can do. Hands are agency: making, holding, grasping, letting go. What the hands are doing in the dream, or unable to do, often mirrors your felt capacity to act on your own life. Notice especially anything the dream has your hands refusing to release.

symbols.name: Eyes / Sight / Blindness
symbols.core_meaning: Consciousness itself: the capacity to see, to know, to perceive truth. Eyes in dreams represent what you can and cannot see about yourself and your situation. Blindness is unconsciousness; clear sight is consciousness; the third eye is spiritual vision.

variations.meaning: Consciousness expanded: you can see what was hidden
Something you cannot or will not see, unconsciousness about a specific area
Being observed by the unconscious: the Self's eye on the ego, or a complex monitoring your behavior
Damage to the capacity for consciousness: something has been hurt that affects your ability to see clearly
A framework for seeing: the particular lens (psychological, spiritual, intellectual) through which you're viewing your experience

symbols.plain_language: What you can and can't see. Dreams about eyes, sight, and blindness tend to track awareness itself: what about your situation is clear, what stays out of view, what you may be choosing not to look at. New glasses, failing vision, a third eye: each shifts the reading.

symbols.name: Hair
symbols.core_meaning: Power, identity, vitality, sexuality, and the part of the body closest to thought. Hair carries enormous symbolic weight across cultures: Samson's strength, a woman's crowning glory, the tonsure of renunciation. In dreams, hair changes often signal identity transformation.

variations.meaning: Loss of vitality, power, or identity: it can feel as if something essential about how you present yourself is being stripped away
Voluntary identity change: cutting away an old identity, renunciation, simplification
Power accumulating, vitality increasing, the wild self growing
Identity transformation: who you are is fundamentally shifting
Confused thoughts, identity knotted, complexity that needs combing through

symbols.plain_language: Identity you can touch. Hair carries vitality, sexuality, and self-image, which is why dream haircuts, hair loss, and sudden new hair tend to accompany identity in transition. For dreamers in treatment or illness, hair dreams often stay close to that lived experience, and deserve a gentle reading.

symbols.name: Wounds / Scars / Bleeding
symbols.core_meaning: The psyche's injuries: where you've been hurt, what hasn't healed, and the Wounded Healer principle that the wound is also the source of healing. A scar is a wound that has healed but left its mark: integrated trauma.

variations.meaning: Something still hurting, unhealed, actively bleeding psychic energy: a complex that hasn't been integrated
Healed wound: the trauma is integrated but its mark remains. Wisdom from suffering.
The moment of wounding: what is hurting you now? The specific injury points toward what is asking for attention.
Integration in process: the injury is closing, the complex is losing its autonomy
The Fisher King wound: a central injury that refuses to close, often the core complex around which individuation revolves

symbols.plain_language: Where it still hurts, and where healing starts. Wounds in dreams tend to show what has been injured and not yet tended. A scar is different: a wound that closed and became part of you. The old idea of the wounded healer says the tended wound can become the very place you help others from.

symbols.name: Pregnancy / Physical Transformation
symbols.core_meaning: Something growing inside that will eventually demand to be born. Pregnancy in dreams, regardless of the dreamer's gender, often represents a creative or psychological development gestating in the unconscious, not yet ready for the world. For dreamers who are pregnant, or who have lost a pregnancy, these dreams often stay close to the lived experience itself and deserve to be read gently.

variations.meaning: A new psychological development is growing: something is gestating that will change your life when it emerges
An unplanned development: something the ego didn't choose is growing anyway. The unconscious has its own creative agenda.
The development is arriving: ready or not, the new content is emerging into consciousness
The psyche is being physically restructured: identity transformation experienced in the body

symbols.plain_language: Something in you is growing. Pregnancy dreams visit dreamers of every gender, and they usually announce a creative or personal development still forming, not ready for the world yet. For dreamers who are pregnant, or who have lost a pregnancy, these dreams often stay close to the lived experience itself and deserve to be read gently.

symbols.name: Blood
symbols.core_meaning: Life force, vitality, lineage, sacrifice, and the cost of being alive. Blood is what circulates, the psyche's living energy. Bloodshed is the price of transformation. Blood ties are the deepest bonds.

variations.meaning: Life force leaking: energy being lost, the cost of an unhealed wound
Guilt, responsibility, having participated in something that drew blood (psychically)
Sacred sacrifice: transformation that requires something to be given up, the alchemical rubedo
Ancestral connection, inherited patterns, what runs in the family psyche
Receiving new life energy from another source: psychic renewal through relationship, therapy, or spiritual practice

symbols.plain_language: Life itself, and its cost. Blood carries vitality, kinship, and sacrifice all at once. Bleeding in a dream can mark energy draining from somewhere in your life; blood shared or given can mark the deepest kind of bond. Where the blood is, and whose, shapes everything.

symbols.name: Fog / Mist
symbols.core_meaning: Obscured consciousness: you can't see clearly. The boundaries between things dissolve. Fog is NOT darkness (unconsciousness): it's DIFFUSED consciousness, where everything is vaguely present but nothing is distinct. The participation mystique: identity boundaries blurred.
symbols.plain_language: Almost seeing. Fog isn't darkness: everything is present but nothing is distinct. Fog dreams tend to come in seasons of real uncertainty, when the shapes of things (a decision, a relationship, a future) haven't resolved yet. The honest move in fog is to slow down, not to pretend you can see.

symbols.name: Snow / Ice / Cold
symbols.core_meaning: Frozen emotion, the psyche in stasis, preservation through cold. Snow beautifies and covers: the Persona's white blanket over the shadow-earth. Ice is emotion hardened into rigidity. Cold is the withdrawal of psychic warmth.

variations.meaning: Quiet covering: a period of rest, stillness, or Persona refreshment. Beautiful but cold.
Overwhelming white-out: consciousness overwhelmed by too much undifferentiated content
Frozen emotion: feelings that have hardened, relationships that have calcified, the Senex's grip
Emotion beginning to flow again after being frozen: spring after winter, feeling returning

symbols.plain_language: Feeling, frozen. Snow softens and covers; ice hardens and preserves. Dreams of cold often track emotional winter: warmth withdrawn, something numbed to get through, a beautiful surface over stopped water. What thaws, or refuses to, is usually the dream's center.

symbols.name: Night / Darkness
symbols.core_meaning: The unconscious as the psyche's natural environment. We dream AT NIGHT: darkness is where the unconscious does its work. Night in dreams is not threatening in itself; it's the condition under which deep content becomes visible, like stars that are always there but invisible in daylight.

variations.meaning: The unconscious as home, comfortable in the darkness, at ease with what can't be seen
Fear of the unconscious: the unknown experienced as danger
The collective unconscious visible: archetypal patterns (stars) shining in the darkness of the psyche
Consciousness emerging from the unconscious: the transition from depth work to waking insight

symbols.plain_language: The dark that isn't against you. Night in a dream is the psyche's home ground: the condition under which deep things become visible, like stars that daylight hides. A night dream isn't automatically a warning. Often it simply means you're in territory the daytime self can't map.

symbols.name: Swimming
symbols.core_meaning: Moving THROUGH the unconscious: not drowning in it, not standing on the shore watching, but actively navigating emotional or unconscious territory. The ego's capacity to engage with depth.

variations.meaning: The ego can navigate the unconscious: therapy is working, dream work is productive, emotional life is manageable
The ego is overwhelmed but still trying: the unconscious is powerful and the ego's capacity is being tested
Voluntary descent into the unconscious: active imagination, deep meditation, choosing to go deeper
The capacity to function IN the unconscious: consciousness that operates in the depths without surfacing. Often a sign of growing ease with the inner world.

symbols.plain_language: In the water, and swimming. Where drowning dreams are about being overwhelmed by feeling, swimming is the opposite report: you're in deep water and moving. These dreams often arrive when you're genuinely engaging with emotional depth rather than avoiding it. The stroke may be effortful. You're still swimming.

symbols.name: Climbing / Ascending
symbols.core_meaning: Effortful upward movement: consciousness working to reach a higher perspective, spiritual aspiration that requires physical (psychic) effort. Unlike flying (effortless, possibly inflated), climbing is earned elevation.

variations.meaning: The individuation journey toward the Self: effortful, requiring endurance, with the goal of perspective and wholeness
Overcoming a barrier: something is blocking upward movement and must be surmounted through effort
Ascending the world tree: moving toward spirit while rooted in nature, the vertical axis of the psyche
The ascent was premature or unsupported: the ego wasn't ready for this height

symbols.plain_language: Height, earned. Unlike flying, climbing gains its altitude one hold at a time: effort, aspiration, the long work toward perspective. A climbing dream often mirrors a real ascent you're in the middle of. The condition of the slope, and whether you can rest, belong to the reading.

symbols.name: Hiding / Concealing
symbols.core_meaning: The ego's defensive response to threatening content: withdrawing from what pursues, concealing what might be seen. Hiding IS the Shadow mechanism: putting things where they can't be found, including yourself.

variations.meaning: Avoiding Shadow confrontation: the ego retreating from what it's not ready to face
Concealing something from consciousness: repression in action
The ego's defense is failing: what was hidden is being found. The Shadow is catching up.
Coming out of hiding: the ego deciding to be seen. Integration moment.

symbols.plain_language: Out of sight, on purpose. Hiding in a dream can be about avoiding something that pursues, or concealing a part of yourself you're not ready to have seen. Worth asking two questions, gently: what are you hiding from, and what of yours is hidden even from you?

symbols.name: Eating / Consuming / Drinking
symbols.core_meaning: Taking something in: metabolizing experience, integrating content, nourishing the psyche. What you eat in a dream is what you're psychologically ingesting. Drinking often connects to the unconscious specifically (water, wine, blood).

variations.meaning: The psyche is starving for something and finally getting it: ravenous intake of needed content
The psyche can't take in what's being offered: something blocks integration
Taking in unconscious content, receiving from the source, spiritual nourishment
Intoxication, ecstasy, Dionysian dissolution of ego boundaries, communion
Being consumed by an unconscious force: the Great Mother devouring, the complex swallowing the ego, Jonah in the whale

symbols.plain_language: Taking the world in. Eating in dreams is integration: experiences, ideas, and feelings being chewed on, swallowed, made part of you. What's on the plate, and whether you can get it down, often mirrors what life is currently asking you to digest.
